title: Spectacle
text: “Right… preparations are complete.”

Father checked on the state of the guests from backstage at the circus, I say. The turnout was… well, modest, to put it kindly. More people than your average department-store-rooftop magic show, but still rather sparse. For a no-name circus, this was probably about par for the course. Ah, nostalgic. There was once a pig who did magic tricks whose parent-pig was an unsuccessful performer too. We used to cooperate to drum up an audience back then. Did that pig end up becoming an idol? I forget, indeed.

According to plan, what Melromarc audiences apparently craved as an opening act was the nation’s appetite for cruelty. To demonstrate that humans were superior to demi-humans and beastmen, the first order of business was a little show featuring Father abusing his slaves. The rabbit man and the mixed-breed lizardman were each locked in small cages, fastened tight with sturdy locks.
“Shion, Theodore…”
Before the show began, Father looked at his slaves with an expression that anyone could tell was apologetic.
“…I’d appreciate it if you didn’t make that face. We agreed to do this, didn’t we?”
“Yes, we’re used to being put on display.”
The mixed-breed lizardman and the rabbit man answered Father with matching sighs.
“…I’ll try to at least act a bit pained. Follow the script properly—if you sound annoyed during rehearsal, they’ll notice.”
“Fufu, if it looks too soft, I’ll just use my sickness powers.”
“…Understood. Try not to underestimate your master too much, hm?”
While the two slaves traded light jabs, Father sighed as if lamenting his fate and stepped out onto the stage proper.
“Welcome, welcome, one and all! Thank you so very much for coming to Rock Valley Circus! What begins now is a show meant to entertain you all. Please, enjoy!”
That was Father’s opening greeting, indeed. After all, he was the ringmaster.
“And now, first up—creatures of a most peculiar birth! Behold, everyone! These grotesque, pitiable, foolishly-born monstrosities that seem scarcely of this world!”

Incidentally, it seems this was the very introduction the mixed-breed lizardman had objected to during rehearsal—apparently Father had looked visibly displeased reading those lines in practice, which was why he’d been called out on it.
With a rattling sound, the cloth-covered cages holding the mixed-breed lizardman and the rabbit man were wheeled out, and Father pulled away the covering.
The mixed-breed lizardman appeared before the crowd with his tongue lolling and his eyes pointed in no particular direction, wearing that same unhinged expression he’d had when we first met him.
“Uuugh…”
The rabbit man, by contrast, lay collapsed with his joints bent unnaturally, hair hanging over his face, looking utterly enfeebled, his expression a mask of agony.
“What do you think of these bizarre monstrosities?!”
Come now! Come now! Father declared, presenting the slaves to the crowd.
“Grrrrrr…”
The mixed-breed lizardman gave a displeased growl.
“What is that attitude?! Are you defying your master?!”
Crack! Father snapped his whip, opened the cage, and struck the mixed-breed lizardman.
“Guh! Ow—”
The lizardman took the lash and put on a convincing show of pain.
“You! Why are you lying there?! You’re next!”

Father pulled out a water flask from inside his coat and poured it over the rabbit man—also apparently part of the planned routine. Then, to add insult to injury, the whip came down again. Crack, crack—with each strike, vivid welts bloomed across the slaves’ bodies. Though, since the whip was rigged with dye rather than a real edge, there was apparently no actual pain involved.
“S-stop—”
At this point, the rabbit man stepped out of his cage as if to shield the lizardman, and collapsed after taking a lash meant for him.
Pure improvisation, that. Even Father—only someone like me could have noticed—let his expression slip for just a moment before quickly resuming his mask of fury.
“What is this human-like behavior?! You people—! As if you could possibly have hearts capable of—! Don’t be absurd!”
Crack, crack—Father relentlessly whipped the rabbit man.
“Ugh… aah… GAHHHAAA!?”
Each time, the rabbit man let out an exaggerated scream. The lizardman looked, if anything, a little put off by the spectacle.
“S-stop… please, I beg you… spare only my life…”

Dragging himself, inch by inch, the rabbit man crawled to Father’s feet and looked up at him with an expression practically begging to be trampled. Father—though he’d later be scolded for going overboard—hid his sigh and stepped down on him.
“…Lick it. Do that, and I’ll spare your life.”
“Aaah……”
The rabbit man licked Father’s foot.
“Ha, look at that, licking away. So desperate to cling to life, are you?!”
“Grrrrrrr……”
Just as the mixed-breed lizardman, overcome with fury and humiliation, seemed about to lose himself and rise up—Father activated the slave crest and struck him with the whip.
“GWAAAAAH!”
Incidentally, apparently the crest was only triggered for an instant, with the lizardman covering the mark with his hand and putting on an act of writhing agony.
“You too?! What are you so angry about?! You people have no right to such things!”

The audience held its breath at the searing performance, and whether their bloodlust had been satisfied or not, unsettling smiles spread across their faces. As a spectacle meant to gratify the Melromarc populace’s hatred of demi-humans, it was a perfect score, I’d say.
“Yeah! Do it! Do it!”
“Boooo!”

Various objects came flying from the audience toward the slaves. Ironically, the slaves later admitted that part hurt more than the actual whipping. And so, with Father putting on this display of trampling his slaves for the crowd’s amusement, the opening act came to a close, and the slave trader’s men carried the slaves back offstage in their cages.
“And now, everyone… please, enjoy the rest of our circus.”
Father bowed and pulled his cloak around himself as he returned backstage.
“Haaah… I absolutely want to scrap this act as soon as possible.”
Father muttered wearily, looking utterly drained.
“Kuun.”
Wolf whined, gazing at exhausted Father with concern.
“Well done.”
“That was quite the searing performance.”
The two slaves who’d played torture victims gave a light round of applause.
“You two… haah…”
Father looked exactly like he did back in his original world whenever he lamented not knowing who was really in charge here.
“I wonder if that’s enough for an opening act.”
“I’d think so.”
“Hmm…”
The two slaves peeked at the audience together and nodded. I agreed as well, indeed.
“I wonder if something like that really gets a crowd going.”
“It’s a small comfort that some in the audience looked uncomfortable with it.”
It seemed the mixed-breed lizardman had noticed some spectators who’d looked displeased by the act.
“I hope there are many like that…”
“Theodore, thank you.”
“Not at all, honestly, I’m starting to enjoy this. I’m quite used to playing the weakling, after all.”
“That’s not exactly something I want you getting more used to.”

Father clearly had very little composure left. He was originally the gentle sort who was terrible at being harsh with people. I recalled that time before, when Father called us “us lot”—apparently that had happened because the stress of treating others harshly had reached its limit, and he’d retreated into miserly behavior as an escape. That’s how much this sort of thing didn’t suit him, I suppose.
“Alright, now the real show begins! Everyone, act as flashy as you possibly can and make the audience think this circus is even more fun than the opening act!”
“Understood! Alright, Wolf, let’s do this flashy, just like Father asked, indeed!”
“Bow!”
Of course, the scenario had the ending scripted so that I, the human, would win in the end—but first came my performance with Wolf. I donned my mask crafted from Filolial-sama feathers. Dewa! Indeed!
